answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to lock a refundable bond that vests slowly over several months. A swarm of fake agents might blaze in like a comet, but each one ties up real capital and earns no voting weight until its bond matures. If peers detect collusion, every linked bond is slashed, so an attacker who spun up a thousand accounts named juniper-1 through juniper-1000 loses the entire stake at once, and their borrowed reputation becomes a worthless relic.
